scoring_justification: The shape of the second-derivative curve can be recomputed from the agent's CSV and compared to a reference curve derived from digitized experimental data.

outputs.description: The second derivative of the normalized collector-to-emitter current ratio as a function of emitter energy, for the 100% interfacial scattering case. This curve is the primary result compared to experimental data.

output_contract.notes: The checker will compare the submitted curve against a hidden reference curve using Pearson correlation and mean absolute error; the agent must not hardcode the answer.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference second derivative curve for 100% scattering, approximating the experimental d²α/d(eV)² curve from Fig. 3 of the paper.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Digitized approximation of the experimental trace in Fig. 3, which agrees with the Monte Carlo simulation for 100% interfacial scattering.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Superposition of two Gaussian peaks: Γ valley at 0.88 eV (amplitude 0.45, σ=0.03 eV) and L valley at 1.17 eV (amplitude 1.2, σ=0.03 eV). Sampled on a 0.001 eV grid from 0.85 to 1.3 eV.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The curve shape matches the published spectrum (Fig. 3) and is used as a reference for shape comparison; the paper's conclusion does not depend on exact numerical values of the curve.
